news.title: Off-Grid Solar Is Now the Cheapest Power for Nearly 400 Million People
news.summary: The World Bank now ranks off-grid solar as the cheapest way to bring electricity to at least 398 million people who still live without it. A joint report released this week by the World Bank’s Energy Sector Management Assistance Program (ESMAP) and the off-grid solar industry association GOGLA treats the technology as permanent infrastructure. Systems once sold as a stopgap until the grid arrived now power households, businesses and factories, and 95% of surveyed customers still had working solar home systems four or more years after buying…

analysis.summary: The World Bank reports that off-grid solar is now the cheapest electricity solution for roughly 400 million people lacking grid access.
analysis.rationale: The expansion of off-grid solar for rural electrification provides basic power to populations without grid infrastructure and has no immediate or material directional implication for global crude oil markets.

news.title: Exxon, Chevron Executives Cancel Gulf Visit Over Security Concerns
news.summary: ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods and Chevron upstream president Clay Neff have canceled plans to attend next week's ADIPEC conference in Abu Dhabi over security concerns, according to sources cited by Reuters on Thursday. Both executives were expected at the November 2-5 event, one of the oil industry's largest annual gatherings, and Woods is still showing up on the roster. Neither company would comment on the cancellations, which come as Washington considers another round of military action against Iran. President Donald Trump has said the United States…

analysis.summary: Exxon and Chevron top executives canceled plans to attend the ADIPEC conference in Abu Dhabi due to security concerns amid potential US military action against Iran.
analysis.rationale: High-level travel cancellations due to regional security threats and possible military escalation involving Iran indicate elevated supply disruption risks in the Persian Gulf, putting upward pressure on crude prices.
